evidence.text: Reason for referral: Evaluation of a new systolic heart murmur found on routine examination in a 64-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension.

Findings: Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm. Normal axis. PR interval 158 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 418 ms. No chamber enlargement.
Impression: Normal sinus rhythm, normal tracing.

Findings: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at 62%. Mild aortic valve sclerosis without stenosis; peak velocity 1.8 m/s. Trace mitral regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Normal left ventricular systolic function. Mild aortic sclerosis without stenosis, likely the source of the murmur.

EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
Neck: no carotid bruits.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur at the upper sternal border, no radiation, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation.
Extremities: no edema.
